title: 思维模型详解：分布式系统思维 · 2026-05-28

questions.question: 一位工程师说：「我们的跨机房系统选了 CA，放弃分区容错，所以既一致又可用。」按对 CAP 的资深理解，问题出在哪？
options: CA 组合能够实现，只是代价高昂，通常只适合预算极其充足的大型系统
跨空间的系统必然断网，P 放弃不了，要选的是断网时保 C 还是 A
三者最多取其二，他应当放弃可用性，换取一致性与分区容错兼得
一致性和可用性天然互斥，即便网络从不中断，两者也不可能同时满足
questions.explanation: 把 CAP 读成「三选二」是初学者误读：分区在跨空间系统里是物理必然，不是可以放弃的选项，真正的问题是分区发生时选 C 还是选 A。网络正常时 C 和 A 并不冲突，而且这个取舍应按操作粒度来做，不是给整个系统贴一个 CP 标签。
questions.question_en: An engineer says: "Our multi-datacenter system chose CA and gave up partition tolerance, so it's both consistent and available." On a mature reading of CAP, what's wrong?
options_en: CA is achievable but expensive, so it generally suits only very large systems with ample budgets
Any system spread across space will lose links, so P isn't optional; the real choice is C or A during a partition
You can have at most two of three, so he should drop availability and keep consistency plus partition tolerance
Consistency and availability are inherently exclusive, so even with a perfect network you can't have both
questions.explanation_en: Reading CAP as "pick two of three" is the novice error: partitions are a physical inevitability in distributed systems, not something you can opt out of, so the real question is C or A when a partition happens. With a healthy network C and A don't conflict, and the trade-off should be made per operation rather than by labeling the whole system CP.

questions.question: 一个团队采用「最终一致」的协作方式：各自先推进、不要求实时同步。几个月后各方信息依然对不上。按最终一致性的思路，最可能缺的是什么？
options: 更多副本：让每个人都保存一份完整的记录以备随时查对
收敛机制：固定的同步点，以及明确的冲突裁决规则
更多时间：最终一致本来就要更久，才能自己慢慢收敛
更强的一致：把关键信息都改成实时全员同步审批
questions.explanation: 「最终」不会自动发生，必须设计收敛机制：何时同步，冲突用什么规则裁决（谁拍板）。没有收敛规则的最终一致只是「永远不一致」，再等多久都不会自己收敛；反过来改成事事实时同步，又回到了拖垮所有人的强一致执念。
questions.question_en: A team works in an "eventually consistent" way: everyone moves ahead without real-time syncing. Months later, people's information still doesn't match. On eventual-consistency thinking, what's most likely missing?
options_en: More replicas: have everyone keep a complete copy of the records for cross-checking
A convergence mechanism: fixed sync points plus a clear rule for resolving conflicts
More time: eventual consistency simply takes longer to converge on its own
Stronger consistency: route all key information through real-time, all-hands approval
questions.explanation_en: "Eventually" doesn't happen for free; you need a convergence mechanism: when to sync and what rule settles conflicts (who decides). Eventual consistency without a convergence rule just means never consistent, however long you wait. Swinging to real-time sync on everything brings back the strong-consistency obsession that bogs everyone down.

questions.question: 一条处理流水线中，下游跟不上上游，任务队列持续增长。哪种应对是在「治本」，并能维持更高的可持续吞吐？
options: 扩大缓冲区，给突发流量留出更大的排队空间，避免丢任务
给下游加上自动重试，确保每条任务最终一定会被处理完
让上游保持全速推送，使瞬时吞吐量最大
下游把拥塞状态回传，上游据此降速，满了就拒绝或延后
questions.explanation: 背压是把下游拥塞回传给上游的负反馈环，主动降速反而能维持更高的可持续吞吐。缓冲只是治标，队列无界增长迟早耗尽内存而雪崩；贪婪地全速接收，崩溃后吞吐直接归零。
questions.question_en: In a processing pipeline the downstream stage can't keep up and the task queue keeps growing. Which response fixes the root cause and sustains higher throughput?
options_en: Enlarge the buffer to give bursts more room to queue, so no tasks are dropped
Add automatic retries downstream so every task is guaranteed to be processed eventually
Keep the producer pushing at full speed to maximize the system's instantaneous throughput
Have downstream signal its congestion upstream so the producer slows, rejecting or deferring when full
questions.explanation_en: Backpressure is a negative-feedback loop that feeds downstream congestion back to the producer, and deliberately slowing down sustains more throughput over time. A buffer only treats the symptom: an unbounded queue eventually exhausts memory and collapses. Greedily accepting everything drives throughput to zero once the system falls over.
